range: Phonetics and phonology, morphemes and phrases, how brains work, brains and language, the Cognitive Revolution, speech errors, experimental design
lead: These pages teach every Module I idea in course order, from speech sounds and morphemes through activation networks, aphasia, the Cognitive Revolution and speech production to experimental design. Each topic explains the reasoning behind the findings, and the review guide answers every prompt on the Midterm 1 review deck.
flags: There is no answer key for LING406, so every answer here is written from the course material.

The pages m1-lecture04-p024 and m1-review-p021 credit the Interactive Activation model to Rumelhart and McClelland (1986), while m1-lecture04-p042 credits it to McClelland and Rumelhart (1981). The accepted dating is McClelland and Rumelhart (1981), so each page keeps its own wording here.

On m1-lecture04-p042 the text says that activation for WORK makes the last letter look more like an R than a K. WORK ends in K, and the letter output plot on the same page has k rising steadily while r stays low. The accepted reading is that word-level support for WORK pushes the ambiguous letter toward K.
On m1-lecture04-p015 the researchers are spelled Hubel and Weisel (1968). The accepted spelling is Hubel and Wiesel, and the cards keep the spelling given.

On m1-lecture09-p002 the text dates Oldfield and Wingfield to 1965, but the reference line on the same page cites Oldfield and Wingfield (1964) in Nature. Both papers exist, and the cards keep the 1965 date from the text.

On m1-lecture07-p009 the text says that whole clusters moving together would have yielded gish frotto. Moving the whole onsets f and gr would give grish fotto, while gish frotto exchanges only f and g. The Fromkin excerpt on the same page lists (6a) as fish grotto becoming frish gotto, and m1-lecture08-p011 later lists gish frotto as a sound-ordering error.

On m1-lecture06-p017 Chomsky's critique is said to predate Marr's work by about a decade. Chomsky's review appeared in 1959 and Marr's Type 1 and Type 2 discussion appeared in 1977, so the gap is closer to two decades.

On m1-lecture06-p003 Turing is said to have built decryption devices for the British Army. Accepted histories place his wartime codebreaking at Bletchley Park for the Government Code and Cypher School, a civilian agency, rather than the Army.

Balota and Lorch used lion as the prime and stripes as the target, as their abstract on m1-review-p025 states. The pages m1-lecture04-p040 and m1-review-p027 describe the reverse direction, stripes priming lion. The network account predicts both, but the tested direction was lion to stripes.
On m1-lecture05-p003 the phrenological faculty is spelled philopropogenitiveness. The accepted spelling is philoprogenitiveness.

On m1-lecture05-p014 the scan is described as H.M.'s middle temporal lobes. H.M.'s surgery removed parts of his medial temporal lobes, so the accepted term is medial temporal lobes, and the notes keep the wording given.
